verses.text: There were false prophets among God’s people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They’ll secretly bring in destructive teachings, even denying the Master who bought them, and bring swift destruction on themselves.
Many will follow their shameless ways, and because of them the way of truth will be slandered.
In their greed they’ll exploit you with made-up stories. Their judgment has been ready for a long time, and their destruction hasn’t been sleeping.
God didn’t spare angels when they sinned. He sent them to Tartarus, putting them in chains of darkness to be held for judgment.
He didn’t spare the ancient world either, but protected Noah, a preacher of righteousness, along with seven others, when he brought the flood on the world of ungodly people.
He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to destruction, reducing them to ashes as an example of what will happen to the ungodly.
But he rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the lawless conduct of those corrupt people.
That righteous man, living among them day after day, was tormented in his righteous soul by the lawless things he saw and heard.
So the Lord knows how to rescue godly people from trials and hold the unrighteous for punishment on judgment day,
especially those who chase after the corrupt desires of their sinful nature and despise authority. They’re bold and arrogant, and they aren’t afraid to insult glorious beings.
Yet angels, though stronger and more powerful, don’t bring insulting charges against those beings before the Lord.
But these people insult what they don’t understand. Like unreasoning animals, born to be caught and destroyed, they’ll be destroyed like animals,

suffering harm as the reward for the harm they’ve done. They think it’s fun to indulge in pleasure during the day. They’re stains and blemishes, delighting in their deceitful pleasures while they feast with you.
Their eyes are full of adultery and never stop sinning. They entice unstable people, and their hearts are trained in greed. They’re under a curse.
They’ve left the straight path and wandered off to follow the path of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the reward for doing wrong.
But he was rebuked for his wrongdoing: a donkey that couldn’t speak used a human voice and restrained the prophet’s madness.
These people are springs without water and mists blown by a storm. The deepest darkness has been reserved for them.
They speak empty, boastful words and use the desires of the flesh to entice people who are just escaping from those who live in error.
They promise freedom while they themselves are slaves of corruption, because people are slaves to whatever has mastered them.
If people have escaped the world’s corruption by knowing our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, but then get tangled up in it again and are conquered, they end up worse than before.
It would have been better for them not to know the way of righteousness than to know it and then turn away from the holy command handed down to them.
What happened to them fits the true proverb: “A dog returns to its vomit,” and, “A washed pig goes back to wallowing in the mud.”
